questions.question: Which statement best describes Snowflake's architecture?

options.text: A shared-nothing architecture where storage and compute are tightly coupled
A multi-cluster, shared-data architecture that separates storage, compute, and cloud services
A single-node architecture optimized for OLTP workloads
A peer-to-peer architecture with no central coordination

explanation.correct: Snowflake uses a multi-cluster, shared-data architecture that separates storage, compute (virtual warehouses), and cloud services so each can scale independently.

whyOthersWrong.a: Snowflake decouples storage and compute rather than tightly coupling them.
whyOthersWrong.c: Snowflake is built for analytical workloads and scales across many nodes.
whyOthersWrong.d: The cloud services layer provides central coordination of metadata and optimization.

questions.question: A virtual warehouse is configured with auto-suspend. What is the primary benefit?

options.text: It permanently deletes unused data to save storage
It pauses compute when idle so you stop paying for unused compute
It automatically increases warehouse size during peak load
It replicates data to another region

explanation.correct: Auto-suspend pauses the warehouse after a period of inactivity, stopping compute billing while it is idle.

whyOthersWrong.a: Auto-suspend affects compute, not stored data.
whyOthersWrong.c: Scaling warehouse size up is a separate resize/scaling concept.
whyOthersWrong.d: Cross-region replication is unrelated to auto-suspend.

questions.question: Which command is used to bulk load data files from a stage into a Snowflake table?

explanation.correct: COPY INTO <table> bulk loads staged files into a target table.

whyOthersWrong.a: INSERT INTO adds individual rows, not bulk file loads from a stage.
whyOthersWrong.b: PUT uploads local files to an internal stage, it does not load into a table.
whyOthersWrong.d: GET downloads files from a stage to a local directory.

questions.question: What is Snowpipe primarily used for?

options.text: Continuous, near-real-time loading of data as files arrive

explanation.correct: Snowpipe enables continuous, micro-batch loading of data shortly after files land in a stage.

whyOthersWrong.b: Role hierarchies are an access-control concept, not loading.
whyOthersWrong.c: Warehouse resizing is a compute operation unrelated to Snowpipe.
whyOthersWrong.d: Encryption at rest is automatic and not Snowpipe's purpose.

questions.question: Which of the following are system-defined roles in Snowflake? (Select TWO)

explanation.correct: ACCOUNTADMIN and SECURITYADMIN are built-in system-defined roles in Snowflake.

whyOthersWrong.b: DATAENGINEER is a custom role name, not system-defined.
whyOthersWrong.d: SUPERUSER is not a Snowflake system-defined role.

questions.question: Which Snowflake feature lets you query or restore data as it existed at an earlier point in time?

explanation.correct: Time Travel lets you access historical data within a configurable retention period.

whyOthersWrong.a: Fail-safe is a Snowflake-managed recovery window after Time Travel expires and is not user-queryable.
whyOthersWrong.c: Snowpipe is for continuous data loading.
whyOthersWrong.d: Clustering organizes data for performance, not historical access.
